html:
The ruins of Yin, the last capital of the Shang dynasty, near Anyang in Henan, northern China. Shang kings ruled from here from about 1250 BCE until the Zhou conquest in about 1046 BCE, a span of twelve kings.

Yinxu is where Chinese history becomes written history. Farmers had long dug up "dragon bones" here and sold them as medicine. In 1899 scholars noticed writing on them. Digs from 1928 found tens of thousands of oracle bones: ox shoulder blades and turtle shells that diviners heated until they cracked, then inscribed with the king's question and the answer. The script is the direct ancestor of Chinese characters.

The site also holds palace foundations, bronze workshops and royal tombs. The tomb of Fu Hao, a queen and general, was found untouched in 1976, with hundreds of bronzes and jades. Large pits of sacrificed people show the darker side of Shang kingship.
